activation.note: Activation retains the adoption gate, declared concrete item scope, normalized top-level comparison, and shorthand/nested/undeclared-key boundaries. It includes unchanged calls and re-evaluation after plan or item-id changes; semantic detection and adoption facts honestly require new observers. The language fact fits the Bun realization.

audit.summary: All 33 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with coder-relevant scope and scan limitations explicit in the coder fields. The application-specific example remains labeled source evidence rather than a new application-specific requirement, and the shared strict-disposition node contains genuinely generic policy text. No undeclared additions or expanded waivers were found.

segmentChecks.note: The core prohibition survives in given/then with the declared-item scope, properties-object target, and forbidden-on-that-item comparison intact.
Then and verifier_detail retain normalized comparison, explicitly including separator stripping, case folding, snake_case plan names, and camelCase code keys.
Given preserves all syntactic bounds: an object literal after the first argument and on the same statement.
Then retains the every-top-level-key scan and both normalization operations; this is not weakened into a raw-name comparison.
Shorthand properties are expressly excluded because they have no name of their own, in both then and activation.doesNotFire.
The nested-object boundary survives; a name appearing only in a nested object is explicitly not a top-level match for the call.
Avoid and verifier_detail preserve the distinction between forbidden and merely undeclared keys and assign undeclared-key drift to the generated contract.
Prefer retains the source's fix direction: pass the identifier rather than the identified thing.
Unless and activation.doesNotFire limit checks to registry-held ids and preserve both raw-string-rule ownership and the double-reporting rationale.
The adoption gate is retained in given, when/activation, unless, and doesNotFire, including its family-wide character.
Strict disposition remains in identity/audit, while shared:policy.strict-disposition preserves the full generic semantics: every finding fails, with no advisory mode or ratchet baseline.

risks: The phrase 'emit-like call' is only glossed as a telemetry emit; someone implementing a new observer would still need the codebase's call-recognition rules, but a coder changing a telemetry emit has enough information to make the correct property decision.

unobservable: The change fact needs a new AST/registry observer for qualifying emit calls, same-statement properties objects, and plan or item-id changes.
The finding fact needs a new bun_telemetry_code forbidden-property observer.
The adopted phase fact needs a new repository adoption observer.

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the prohibition, normalization, scan boundaries, exceptions, adoption gate, and strict disposition without expanding scope. Coder-facing guidance is sufficient for correct implementation, and the activation conditions are deterministic once their honestly declared observers are available; I agree with the auditor's PASS.
